title: The Saltmere Winch
premise: The village of Saltmere wants its silting harbor dredged before the autumn trade ships arrive. Overnight, the dredger's winch cable was cut and its pins knocked loose. You are a stranger sent to find out who did it.

places.name: Harbor Quay
places.description: A stone quay slick with morning damp. The dredger sits idle at its mooring, its winch hanging slack.

places.name: Harbormaster's Office
places.description: A cramped room of ledgers, tide tables and a stove that has gone cold.

places.name: Fish Market
places.description: Trestle tables under a tarred awning, with a small dock behind for the skiffs.

places.name: Chandlery
places.description: Rope, lamp oil and iron tools, each shelf labelled in a careful hand.

places.name: The Salt Cask
places.description: A low-beamed tavern that smells of smoke and last night's ale.

places.name: Lighthouse
places.description: A whitewashed tower on the point. From the gallery the whole harbor lies open.

characters.name: Odrin Vale
characters.persona: Gruff and tired. Wants the dredging done.
characters.speech_style: Short, blunt sentences. Little patience for small talk.
characters.fallback_line: I've a harbor to run. Ask me something I can answer.

characters.name: Mira Tolle
characters.persona: Warm, up at all hours, always with a net in her lap.
characters.speech_style: Talks in half-finished thoughts that trail off and circle back.
characters.fallback_line: Oh, I... no, I've lost the thread of it. These nets won't mend themselves.

characters.name: Tom Brask
characters.persona: Jovial and evasive. Has a bad knee. Claims he was home asleep all night.
characters.speech_style: Loud, friendly, quick to change the subject to fish.
characters.fallback_line: Ha! You'll get no gossip from me, friend. Mackerel's fresh, though.

characters.name: Ysolde Crane
characters.persona: Precise and guarded about her customers.
characters.speech_style: Measured and exact. Answers the question asked and no more.
characters.fallback_line: I don't discuss my customers' purchases.

characters.name: Bram Oyle
characters.speech_style: Few words, long pauses, plain observations.
characters.fallback_line: Couldn't say. I only watch the water.

characters.name: Hale Pruitt
characters.persona: A gossip who knows everyone's business and resents the harbor fees.
characters.speech_style: Chatty and confiding, leans in as if sharing a secret.
characters.fallback_line: Now that I couldn't tell you. Another drink while you think on it?

clues.text: The winch cable was cut clean, and the pins were knocked loose.
Tom spoke loudly against dredging at last week's town meeting ("bigger ships, smaller catch").
A figure with a limp and a lantern walked the quay near 2 a.m. toward the fish market.
A small unlit skiff left the fish market dock around 1:30 and returned around 2:30.
Ysolde sold bolt cutters to Tom two days ago, paid in fish.
Tom left the tavern at midnight, complaining about his knee.
Hale argued with Odrin over unpaid harbor fees and said he would "see the harbor sink".
The tavern was lit and noisy until about 3 a.m., and Hale never left the bar.
Tom admits he cut the cable: bigger ships would end his monopoly selling to the small boats.

pointers.line: Ask Mira. She's up all hours.
If anyone wished this harbor ill, it's Hale Pruitt.
Ask Bram. The lighthouse sees the water.
Anyone cutting a cable needed cutters. Ysolde sells them.
Odrin chaired that meeting. He'll tell you who shouted loudest.

solution.motive: Bigger ships would end his monopoly selling to the small boats.
solution.method: He cut the cable with bolt cutters bought from Ysolde.
true_timeline: 01:30 He takes the skiff from the fish market dock.
About 02:00 he walks back along the quay with a lantern.
